Holy days and Sabbath bell,
Richest, brightest, sweetest treasure,
Can I say a last farewell?
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Yes, my native land, I love thee,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 385b (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Christ Our Song
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Awake my heart, arise my tongue,
Prepare a tuneful voice;
In God, the life of all my joys,
Aloud will I rejoice.
When I appear in yonder cloud,
With all the sacred throng;
Then will I sing more sweet, more loud,
And Christ will be my song.
hymns.first_line: Awake my heart, arise my tongue,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 386 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Penick
stanzas:
While trav’ling through the world below,
Where sore afflictions come,
My soul abounds with joy to know
That I will rest at home.
Chorus:

My soul’s delight has been to sing
Of glorious days to come,
When I shall, with my God and King,
Forever rest at home.
(Chorus)

Yes when my eyes are closed in death,
My body cease to roam,
I’ll bid farewell to all below,
And meet my friends at home.
(Chorus)

And then I want these lines to be
Inscribed upon my tomb,
“Here lies the dust of SRP,
His spirit sings at home.”
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: While trav’ling through the world below,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 387 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Happy Sailor
hymns.author: Verses 2 & 3 C. J. Griggs, 1911
stanzas:
Come, tell of your ship and what is her name?
Oh, tell me, happy sailor!
Come, tell of your captain and what is his name?
Oh, tell me, happy sailor!
Chorus:

She’s the old ship of Zion, hallelu!
And her captain, Judah’s Lion, hallelujah.

Say, is her keel sound, her garner well stored?
Oh, tell me, happy sailor!
And will she leave other comrades on board?
Oh, tell me, happy sailor!
(Chorus)

She will land us safe on Canaan’s bright shore,
Oh, glory, hallelujah!
We’ll land with our friends, who’ve gone on before,
Oh, glory, hallelujah!
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Come, tell of your ship and what is her name?
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 388 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Fredericksburg
stanzas:
I need God’s blessings while I live,
And His undying love;
And then I want to sing His praise
In that sweet home above.
hymns.first_line: I need God’s blessings while I live,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 389 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Prospect
stanzas:
Oh land of rest, for thee I sigh:
When will the moment come
When I shall lay my armor by,
And dwell in peace at home?

No tranquil joy on earth I know,
No peaceful, sheltering dome;
This world’s a wilderness of woe,
This world is not my home.
This world’s a wilderness of woe,
Oh this is not my home.

Our tears shall all be wiped away
When we have ceased to roam,
And we shall hear our Father say,
Come dwell with me at home.
hymns.first_line: Oh land of rest, for thee I sigh:
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 390 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sounding Joy
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Behold the morning sun
Begins his glorious way,
His beams through all the nations run,
And light and life convey.

But when the gospel comes,
It spreads diviner light,
It calls dead sinners from their tombs,
And gives the blind their sight.

My gracious God, how plain
Are Thy directions giv’n,
Oh, may I never read in vain,
But find the path to heav’n.
hymns.first_line: Behold the morning sun
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 391 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Manchester
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
There is a land of pure delight,
Where saints immortal reign;
Infinite day excludes the night,
And pleasures banish pain.
There everlasting spring abides,
And never with’ring flow’rs;
Death like a narrow sea divides
This heav’nly land from ours.

There I shall bathe my weary soul
In seas of heav’nly rest,
And not a wave of trouble roll
Across my peaceful breast.
When we’ve been there ten thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun;
We’ve no less days to sing God’s praise
Than when we first begun.
hymns.first_line: There is a land of pure delight,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 392 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Alexander
hymns.author: Timothy R. Gilmore, 1986
hymns.first_line: Jesus, my Shepherd, Friend, and Guide
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 393 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Messiah’s Praise
hymns.author: Benjamin Rhodes, 1787
hymns.composer: R. F. M. Mann & James A. Sparks, 1869
stanzas:
My heart and voice I raise
To spread Messiah’s praise;
Let all repeat the universal Lord.
Praise Him by whose almighty word,
Creation rose in form complete.
hymns.first_line: My heart and voice I raise
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 394 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Bethel
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1739
stanzas:
Oh for a thousand tongues to sing
My great Redeemer’s praise;
The glories of my God and King,
The triumphs of His grace.
My gracious Master and my God,
Assist me to proclaim,
To spread through all the earth abroad
The honors of Thy name.

Jesus, the name that charms our fears,
That bids our sorrows cease;
’Tis music in the sinner’s ears,
’Tis life and health and peace.
He breaks the pow’r of canceled sin,
He sets the pris’ner free;
His blood can make the foulest clean
His blood availed for me.
hymns.first_line: Oh for a thousand tongues to sing
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 395 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Notes Almost Divine
hymns.author: Samuel Medley, 1789
stanzas:
Oh, could I speak the matchless worth,
Oh, could I sound the glories forth,
Which in my Savior shine.
I’d soar and touch the heav’nly strings,
And vie with Gabriel while he sings,
In notes almost divine.

Well, the delightful day will come,
When my dear Lord will take me home,
And I shall see His face.
Then with my Savior, Brother, Friend,
A blest eternity I’ll spend,
Triumphant in His grace.
hymns.first_line: Oh, could I speak the matchless worth,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 396 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Fountain
hymns.author: William Cowper, 1772
stanzas:
There is a fountain filled with blood,
Drawn from Immanuel’s veins;
And sinners plunged beneath that flood,
Lose all their guilty stains.
The dying thief rejoiced to see
That fountain in his day;
And there may I, though vile as he,
Wash all my sins away.

E’er since by faith I saw the stream,
Thy flowing wounds supply;
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die.
Then in a nobler, sweeter song,
I’ll sing Thy pow’r to save,
When this poor lisping, stamm’ring tongue
Lies silent in the grave.
hymns.first_line: There is a fountain filled with blood,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 397 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Dying Boy
stanzas:
I’m dying, Mother, dying now;
Please raise my aching head,
And fan my heated, burning brow,
Your boy will soon be dead.
Turn o’er my pillow once again,
And kiss my fevered cheek;
I’ll soon be freed from all the pain,
For now I am so weak.
hymns.first_line: I’m dying, Mother, dying now;
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 398 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Dying Friend
hymns.author: Lee Wells, 1935
stanzas:
Young people, hear me as your friend,
Whose days on earth are at an end;
Your talents to the Savior lend
And live forevermore.

His Word will guide you here below,
Great love and mercy He will show;
And then with Jesus you may go
And live forevermore.

With you no longer I may dwell,
But His great love for you I tell;
I’m ready now to bid farewell
And live forevermore.
hymns.first_line: Young people, hear me as your friend,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 399t (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Happy Christian
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1749
stanzas:
Oh, how happy are they,
Who their Savior obey,
And have laid up their treasures above;
Tongue can never express
The sweet comfort and peace,
Of a soul in its earliest love.

That sweet comfort was mine
When the favor divine,
I first found in the blood of the Lamb;
When at first I believed,
What true joy I received,
What a haven in Jesus’ sweet name.

’Twas a heaven below,
My Redeemer to know,
And the angels could do nothing more;
Than to fall at His feet
And the story repeat
And the lover of sinners adore.
hymns.first_line: Oh, how happy are they,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 399b (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Struggle On
stanzas:
Our praying time will soon be o’er, Hallelujah,
We’ll join with those gone on before, Hallelujah.
Chorus:

Struggle on, struggle on, Hallelujah,
Struggle on, for the work’s most done, Hallelujah.

To love and bless and praise the same, Hallelujah,
Of Jesus Christ, the bleeding Lamb, Hallelujah.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Our praying time will soon be o’er, Hallelujah,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 400 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Cuba
hymns.composer: J. H. Bolen & H. S. Reese, 1859
stanzas:
Go, preachers, and tell it to the world,
Poor mourners found a home at last.
Chorus:

Through free grace and a dying Lamb,
Poor mourners found a home at last.

Go, fathers, and tell it to the world,
Poor mourners found a home at last.
(Chorus)

Go, mothers, and tell it to the world,
Poor mourners found a home at last.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Go, preachers, and tell it to the world,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 401 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Heavenly Rest
hymns.author: Augustus M. Toplady, 1759
stanzas:
How happy are the souls above,
From sin and sorrow free;
With Jesus they are now at rest,
And all His glory see.
hymns.first_line: How happy are the souls above,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 403 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Youth Will Soon Be Gone
hymns.author: New England Sunday School Hymn Book, 1830
stanzas:
Youth, like the spring, will soon be gone,
By fleeting time or conqu’ring death;
Your morning sun may set at noon,
And leave you ever in the dark.
Your sparkling eyes and blooming cheeks
Must wither like the blasted rose;
The coffin, earth, and winding sheet
Will soon your active limbs enclose.

Ye heedless ones who wildly stroll,
The grave will soon become your bed,
Where silence reigns and vapors roll,
In solemn darkness ’round your head.
Your friends will pass the lonesome place,
And with a sigh move slowly on,
Still gazing on the spires of grass
With which your graves are overgrown.

Ye blooming youth, this is the state
Of all who do free grace refuse;
And soon with you ’twill be too late
The way of life and Christ to choose.
Come lay your carnal weapons by,
No longer fight against your God;
But with the gospel now comply,
And heav’n shall be your great reward.
hymns.first_line: Youth, like the spring, will soon be gone,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 404 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Marcellas
hymns.author: John Cennick, 1742
stanzas:
Children of the heav’nly King,
As we journey, sweetly sing;
Sing your Savior’s worthy praise.
Glorious in His works and ways.

Fear not, brethren — joyful stand
On the borders of your land;
Jesus Christ, your Father’s Son,
Bids you undismayed go on.

Lord, submissive make us go,
Gladly leaving all below;
Only Thou our leader be,
And we still will follow Thee.
hymns.first_line: Children of the heav’nly King,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 405 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Harmony
hymns.author: The Sacred Harp, 1859
stanzas:
I want to live a Christian here,
I want to die a-shouting.
I want to feel my Savior near,
While soul and body’s parting.
I want to see bright angels stand
And waiting to receive me,
To bear my soul to Canaan’s land,
Where Christ has gone before me.

My heart is often made to mourn
Because I’m faint and feeble,
And when my Savior seems to frown,
My soul is filled with trouble.
But when He doth again return,
And I repent my folly,
’Tis then I after glory run,
And still my Jesus follow.

I have my bitter and my sweet
While through this world I travel,
Sometimes I shout and often weep,
Which makes my foes to marvel.
But let them think and think again,
I feel I’m bound for heaven;
I hope I shall with Jesus reign,
I therefore still will praise Him.
hymns.first_line: I want to live a Christian here,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 406 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Charlton
hymns.author: Frances Maria Cowper, 1792
stanzas:
My span of life will soon be gone
The passing moments say;
As length’ning shadows o’er the mead
Proclaim the close of day.
Oh, that my heart might dwell aloof
From all created things,
And learn that wisdom from above
Whence true contentment springs.

Ere first I drew this vital breath,
From nature’s prison free,
Crosses in number, measure, weight,
Were written, Lord, for me.
But Thou my Shepherd, Friend, and Guide,
Hast kindly led me on,
Taught me to rest my fainting head
On Christ, the Cornerstone.
hymns.first_line: My span of life will soon be gone
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 407 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Promised Day
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
How long, dear Savior, Oh how long
Shall this bright hour delay?
Fly swift around, ye wheels of time,
And bring the promised day.

The God of glory down to men
Removes His blest abode;
Men, the dear object of His grace,
And He the living God.

His own soft hand shall wipe the tears
From ev’ry weeping eye,
And pains and groans and griefs and fears
And death itself shall die.
hymns.first_line: How long, dear Savior, Oh how long
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 409 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Dying Californian
hymns.author: Kate Harris, 1850
stanzas:
Lay up nearer, brother, nearer,
For my limbs are growing cold;
And thy presence seemeth nearer,
When thine arms around me fold.

I am dying, brother, dying,
Soon you’ll miss me in your berth
For my form will soon be lying
’Neath the ocean’s briny surf.

I am going, brother, going,
But my hope in God is strong;
I am willing, brother, knowing,
That He doeth nothing wrong.

Hark! I hear the Savior speaking,
’Tis, I know, His voice so well;
When I’m gone, Oh don’t be weeping,
Brother, hear my last farewell.
hymns.first_line: Lay up nearer, brother, nearer,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 410t (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Mutual Love
hymns.author: John Leland, 1793
stanzas:
Oh when shall I see Jesus
And reign with Him above,
And from the flowing fountain
Drink everlasting love?
When shall I be delivered
From this vain world of sin,
And with my blessed Jesus
Drink endless pleasures in?

But now I am a soldier,
My Captain’s gone before;
He’s given me my orders,
And bids me ne’er give o’er.
His promises are faithful —
A righteous crown He’ll give,
And all His valiant soldiers
Eternally shall live.
hymns.first_line: Oh when shall I see Jesus
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 410b (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Morning Prayer
hymns.author: Hosea Ballou, 1808
stanzas:
Come, let us raise our voices high,
And form a sacred song,
To Him who rules the earth and sky,
And does our days prolong.
Who through the night gave us to rest,
This morning cheered our eyes;
And with the thousands of the blest,
In health made us to rise.

Early to God we’ll send our prayer,
Make haste to pray and praise,
That He may make our good His care,
And guide us all our days.
And when the night of death comes on,
And we shall end our days;
May His rich grace the theme prolong
Of His eternal praise.
hymns.first_line: Come, let us raise our voices high,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 411 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Hosanna
hymns.author: Dobell’s New Selection, 1806
stanzas:
Wake, Oh my soul, and hail the morn,
For unto us a Savior’s born:
See how the angels wing their way
To usher in the glorious day.
Chorus:

Glory, glory, let us sing,
While heav’n and earth His praises ring,
Hosanna to the Lamb of God.

Hark! what sweet music, what a song,
Sounds from the bright celestial throng;
Sweet song, whose melting sounds impart
Joy to each raptured list’ning heart.
(Chorus)

Come, join the angels in the sky,
Glory to God who reigns on high;
Let peace and love on earth abound,
While time revolves and years roll ’round.
hymns.first_line: Wake, Oh my soul, and hail the morn,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 412 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Loved Ones
stanzas:
Be kind to thy father, for when thou wert young,
Who loved thee so fondly as he?
He caught the first accent that fell from thy tongue,
And joined in thy innocent glee.
Be kind to thy father, for now he is old,
His locks intermingled with gray;
His footsteps are feeble, once fearless and bold,
Thy father is passing away.
hymns.first_line: Be kind to thy father, for when thou wert young,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 413 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Parting Friend
stanzas:
The time must come when we must part,
When we must say farewell;
To part with you gives to my heart
A sting no one can tell.
When I am gone and far away,
I still will think of thee.
I’ll think of thee both night and day,
Oh then remember me.
hymns.first_line: The time must come when we must part,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 414 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Easter Morn
hymns.author: St.1 Lyra Davidica, 1708 & St.2 Thomas Scott, 1769
stanzas:
Jesus Christ is ris’n today,
Hallelujah!
Or triumphant holy day,
Hallelujah!
Who did once upon the cross,
Hallelujah!
Suffer to redeem our loss,
Hallelujah!

Angels rolled the rock away,
Hallelujah!
Den of death, resign thy prey,
Hallelujah!
See the Savior quit the tomb,
Hallelujah!
Glowing with immortal bloom,
Hallelujah!
hymns.first_line: Jesus Christ is ris’n today,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 415 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Christian’s Nightly Song
hymns.author: Mead’s General Collection, 1807
stanzas:
I’ll sing my Savior’s grace,
And His sweet name I’ll praise,
While in this land of sorrow I remain.
My sorrows soon shall end,
And then my soul ascend,
Where freed from trouble, sorrow and pain.

But oh, and shall I then
Behold the friend of men,
The man who suffered, bled and died for me:
Who bore my load of sin,
And sorrow, grief and pain
To make me happy and to set me free.
hymns.first_line: I’ll sing my Savior’s grace,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 416 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Weeping Pilgrim
stanzas:
You may tell them, father,
When you see them —
Chorus:

I’m a poor, mourning Pilgrim,
I’m bound for Canaan’s land.
I weep, and I mourn,
And I move slowly on —
I’m a poor, mourning Pilgrim,
I’m bound for Canaan’s land.

You may tell them, mother,
When you see them —
(Chorus)

You may tell them, brother,
When you see them —
(Chorus)

You may tell them, sister,
When you see them —
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: You may tell them, father,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 417 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Reese
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709
stanzas:
There is a house not made with hands,
Eternal, and on high;
And here my spirit waiting stands,
Till God shall bid it fly.
Chorus:

I long to see my friends again,
And hear them sweetly say,
Come, weary dove, here is thy home,
Then fold thy wings and stay.

Shortly this prison of clay
Must be dissolved and fall;
Then, Oh my soul, with joy obey
Thy heav’nly Father’s call.
(Chorus)

’Tis He, by His almighty grace,
That forms thee fit for heav’n;
And as an earnest of the place,
Has His own Spirit giv’n.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: There is a house not made with hands,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 418 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Melancholy Day
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709
stanzas:
Death, ’tis a melancholy day,
To those who have no God,
When the poor soul is forced away,
To seek her last abode.
In vain to heav’n she lifts her eyes,
For guilt, a heavy chain,
Still drags her downward from the skies,
To darkness, fire and pain.
hymns.first_line: Death, ’tis a melancholy day,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 419 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Bishop
hymns.author: Octavia Bishop McGraw, 1935
stanzas:
Our Father’s gone to that bright land,
He dwells with Christ, the King;
And with the saints of old doth stand,
While all the angels sing.

Around dear Mother’s bed we stood
And watched her dying face;
While Jesus bade her spirit come
And take a heav’nly place.

Their forms on earth no more we see,
They’re hidden from our view;
Their mem’ries linger still with me,
As noble, good and true.

Could we but stand and view that goal,
’Twould dry our briny tears;
True love and joy there to behold,
Would banish all our fears.
hymns.first_line: Our Father’s gone to that bright land,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 420 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sweet Morning
stanzas:
The happy day will soon appear,
And we’ll all shout together in that morning.
When Gabriel’s trumpet you shall hear,
And we’ll all shout together in that morning.
Chorus:

Sweet morning, sweet morning,
And we’ll all shout together in that morning.

Behold the righteous marching, home,
And we’ll all shout together in that morning.
And all the angels bid them come,
And we’ll all shout together in that morning.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: The happy day will soon appear,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 421 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Burdette
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1742
stanzas:
Oh, for a heart to praise my God,
A heart from sin set free,
A heart made clean by Thy rich blood,
So freely shed for me.
hymns.first_line: Oh, for a heart to praise my God,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 422 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Grantville
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Should earth against my soul engage,
And fiery darts be hurled,
Then I can smile at Satan’s rage,
And face a frowning world.
hymns.first_line: Should earth against my soul engage,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 423 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sweet Union
hymns.author: Samuel Medley, 1782
stanzas:
Awake, my soul, to joyful lays,
Oh, glory, hallelujah!
And sing thy great Redeemer’s praise,
Don’t you love God!
Oh, glory, hallelujah!
Chorus:

There’s union in heav’n,
And there’s union in my soul,
Oh, glory, hallelujah!
Sweet music in Zion’s beginning to roll,
Don’t you love God!
Oh, glory, hallelujah!

He saw me ruined by the fall,
Yet loved me, notwithstanding all;
(Chorus)

I often feel my sinful heart,
Prone from my Savior to depart,
(Chorus)

But though I have Him oft forgot,
His loving kindness changes not!
hymns.first_line: Awake, my soul, to joyful lays,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 424 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Golden Streets
stanzas:
I am on my journey home,
To the New Jerusalem.
hymns.first_line: I am on my journey home,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 425 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Kelley
hymns.author: Amanda Burdette Denson, 1908
stanzas:
My Christian friends, to whom I speak,
I have a crown in view.
My sinner friends, now will you seek,
How stands the case with you?
I know there is a paradise,
The saints all bid us come.
And He who reigns rules earth and sky,
Oh heaven is my home.
hymns.first_line: My Christian friends, to whom I speak,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 426t (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Jasper
hymns.author: Ottiwell Heginbotham, 1794
stanzas:
Great God, let all Thy tuneful pow’r
Away and sing Thy praise,
I’ll sing God’s praise through endless days,
And live forevermore.
Behold the love the Savior showed
When He died upon the cross for sinners,
And whosoever will believe on Jesus’ word
Shall live and sing His praise above,
Through endless days to come,
In heav’n above, where all is love,
To live forevermore.
hymns.first_line: Great God, let all Thy tuneful pow’r
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 426b (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: World Unknown
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1763
stanzas:
And am I born to die?
To lay this body down!
And must my trembling spirit fly
Into a world unknown?

Waked by the trumpet sound,
I from my grave shall rise;
And see the Judge with glory crowned,
And see the flaming skies!
hymns.first_line: And am I born to die?
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 428 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Christian’s Delight
hymns.author: Samuel Ecking, 1778
stanzas:
Peace, troubled soul, thou need not veer,
Jesus says He will be with us to the end.
Thy Great Provider still is near,
Jesus says He will be with us to the end.
Chorus:

And He has been with us,
And He yet is with us,
And He’s promised to be with us to the end.

Who fed thee last, will feed thee still,
Be calm and sink into His will.
(Chorus)

The Lord, who build the earth and sky,
In mercy stoops to hear thy cry.
(Chorus)

His promise all may freely claim,
Ask, and receive in Jesus’ name.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Peace, troubled soul, thou need not veer,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 429 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Arbacoochee
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Behold the love, the gen’rous love,
That holy David shows,
Behold his kind compassion move
For his afflicted foes.
When they are sick, his soul complains,
And seems to feel the smart.
The spirit of the gospel reigns,
And melts his pious heart.
hymns.first_line: Behold the love, the gen’rous love,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 430 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Bethany
hymns.author: Harriet Auber, 1829
stanzas:
Ere mountains reared their forms sublime,
Or heav’n and earth in order stood;
Before the birth of ancient times,
From everlasting, Thou art God.
hymns.first_line: Ere mountains reared their forms sublime,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 431 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Cheves
hymns.author: Baptist Hymn Book, 1825
stanzas:
Grace, ’tis a most delightful theme,
’Tis grace that rescues guilty man,
’Tis grace divine, all conquering free,
Or it had never rescued me.
hymns.first_line: Grace, ’tis a most delightful theme,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 432 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: McKay
hymns.author: Samuel Stennett, 1787
stanzas:
Oh, the transporting, rapturous scene
That rises to my sight!
Sweet fields arrayed in living green,
And rivers of delight.
There gen’rous fruits that never fail
On trees immortal grow,
There rocks and hills and brooks and vales
With milk and honey flow.
hymns.first_line: Oh, the transporting, rapturous scene
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 433 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Fillmore
hymns.author: Ottiwell Heginbotham, 1794
stanzas:
Great God, let all my tuneful pow’rs
Awake, and sing Thy mighty name;
Thy hand revolves my circling hours,
Thy hand from whence my being come.
Thus will I sing till nature cease,
Till sense and language are no more,
And after death Thy boundless grace
Through everlasting years adore.
hymns.first_line: Great God, let all my tuneful pow’rs
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 434 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sacred Rest
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Sweet is the day of sacred rest,
No mortal care shall fill my breast;
Oh, may my heart in tune be found,
Like David’s harp of solemn sound.
hymns.first_line: Sweet is the day of sacred rest,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 435 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Morning Sun
hymns.author: New England Sunday School Hymn Book, 1830
stanzas:
Youth, like the spring, will soon be gone,
By fleeting time or conqu’ring death;
Your morning sun may set at noon,
And leave you ever in the dark.
Your sparkling eyes and blooming cheeks
Must wither like the blasted rose;
The coffin, earth, and winding sheet
Will soon your active limbs enclose.
hymns.first_line: Youth, like the spring, will soon be gone,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 436 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sidney
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
My Shepherd will supply my need,
Jehovah is His name,
In pastures green He leads me on,
Beside the living stream.
With loving kindness Thou hast drawn
My wand’ring heart to Thee.
With kind compassion send me on
To all eternity.
hymns.first_line: My Shepherd will supply my need,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 437 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Marriage in the Skies
hymns.author: Sidney Burdette Denson, 1909
stanzas:
Oh ring the bells of heaven high,
The marriage feast has come,
The glorious jubilee is nigh,
The saints are going home;
The mighty pennants of the skies
Are waving in the air,
And o’er the gates of Zion rise
The battlements so fair.

From cloud to cloud, from dome to dome,
The myriad army cries,
The marriage of the Lamb has come,
The marriage in the skies;
Come, bring the linen white and clean,
The wedding guests prepare,
The garments gleam like silvery sheen,
The bridal robe so fair.

The Bridegroom, too, methinks I see
While myriad voices ring,
Chiefest among ten thousand,
He Immanuel, my King,
Thrice blessed are they who hear the call,
A mighty angel cries,
Haste to the supper of the Lamb,
The marriage in the skies.
hymns.first_line: Oh ring the bells of heaven high,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 438 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Jordan (Second)
hymns.author: Samuel Stennett, 1787
stanzas:
On Jordan’s stormy banks I stand,
And cast a wishful eye,
To Canaan’s fair and happy land
Where my possessions lie.
Oh, the transporting, rapturous scene
That rises to my sight!
Sweet fields arrayed in living green,
And rivers of delight.
hymns.first_line: On Jordan’s stormy banks I stand,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 439 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: North Salem
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
My soul, come and meditate the day,
And think how near it stands,
When thou must quit this house of clay,
And fly to unknown lands.

And you, mine eyes, look down and view
The hollow, gaping tomb,
This gloomy prison waits for you,
Whene’er the summons come.
hymns.first_line: My soul, come and meditate the day,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 440 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Raymond
hymns.author: Philip Doddridge, 1755
stanzas:
Hark, the glad sound! the Savior comes,
The Savior promised long;
Let every heart prepare a throne,
And every voice a song.

He comes, the pris’ner to release,
In Satan’s bondage held;
The gates of brass before Him burst,
The iron fetters yield.
hymns.first_line: Hark, the glad sound! the Savior comes,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 441 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Jordan
hymns.author: Samuel Stennett, 1787
stanzas:
On Jordan’s stormy banks I stand,
And cast a wishful eye,
To Canaan’s fair and happy land
Where my possessions lie.
Oh the transporting, rapturous scene
That rises to my sight!
Sweet fields arrayed in living green,
And rivers of delight.

There gen’rous fruits that never fail,
On trees immortal grow;
There rocks and hills and brooks, and vales,
With milk and honey flow.
All o’er those wide, extended plains
Shines one eternal day!
There God the Son forever reigns,
And scatters night away.
hymns.first_line: On Jordan’s stormy banks I stand,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 442 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Passing Away
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1763
stanzas:
And must I be to judgment brought,
And answer in that day
For ev’ry vain and idle thought
And ev’ry word I say?
Chorus:

We are passing away,
To that great judgment day.

Yes ev’ry secret of my heart
Shall shortly be made known;
And I receive my just desert
For all that I have done.
(Chorus)

How careful, then, ought I to be;
With what religious fear,
Who such a strict account must give
For my behavior here.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: And must I be to judgment brought,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 445 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Infinite Day
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
There is a land of pure delight,
Where saints immortal reign,
Infinite day excludes the night,
And pleasures banish pain.
There everlasting spring abides,
And never with’ring flow’rs;
Death, like a narrow sea, divides
This heav’nly land from ours.

Sweet fields beyond the swelling flood,
Stand dressed in living green,
So to the Jews old Canaan stood,
While Jordan rolled between.
But tim’rous mortals start and shrink
To cross this narrow sea,
And linger, shiv’ring on the brink,
And fear to launch away.

Oh! could we make our doubts remove,
Those gloomy doubts that rise,
And see the Canaan that we love
With unbeclouded eyes.
Could we but climb where Moses stood
And view the landscape o’er,
Not Jordan’s stream nor death’s cold flood
Should fright us from the shore.
hymns.first_line: There is a land of pure delight,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 446 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Wondrous Cross
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
When I survey the wondrous cross
On which the Prince of glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.
Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the death of Christ, my God;
All the vain things that charm me most,
I sacrifice them to His blood.

See, from His head, His hands, His feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down!
Did e’er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?
Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so amazing, so divine,
Demands my soul, my life, my all.
hymns.first_line: When I survey the wondrous cross
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 447 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Consecration
hymns.author: William S. Turner, 1866
stanzas:
There then to Thee Thine own I leave,
Mold as Thou wilt my passive clay;
But let me all Thy stamp receive,
But let me all Thy words obey.
Serve with a single heart and eye,
And to Thy glory live or die.
hymns.first_line: There then to Thee Thine own I leave,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 448t (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Grieved Soul
hymns.author: Joseph Hart, 1759
stanzas:
Come, my soul and let us try
For a little season
Ev’ry burden to lay by,
Come and let us reason.
What is this that casts thee down?
Who are those that grieve thee?
Speak and let the worst be known?
Speaking may relieve thee.
hymns.first_line: Come, my soul and let us try
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 448b (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Fatherland
hymns.author: William Hunter, 1842
hymns.composer: Samuel Wakefield & Arr. Silas W. Kay, 1855
stanzas:
There is a place where my hopes are stayed,
My heart and my treasures are there,
Where virtues and blessings never face,
And fields are eternally fair.
That blissful place is my fatherland,
By faith its delights I explore,
Come, favor my flight, angelic band,
And waft me in peace to the shore.
hymns.first_line: There is a place where my hopes are stayed,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 449 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Elder
hymns.author: American Sunday School Psalmody, 1832
stanzas:
Gently glides the stream of life,
Oft along the flow’ry vale.
Or impetuous down the cliff,
Rushing roars when storms assail.
Life’s an ever varied flood,
Always rolling to its sea;
Slow, or quick, or mild, or rude,
Tending to eternity.
hymns.first_line: Gently glides the stream of life,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 450 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Mary’s Grief and Joy
hymns.author: John Newton, 1779
hymns.composer: J. P. Webster & Arr. B. F. White, 1869
stanzas:
Mary to her Savior’s tomb
Hasted at the early dawn;
Spice she brought and sweet perfume,
But the Lord she loved was gone.

For awhile she weeping stood,
Struck with sorrow and surprise;
Shedding tears, a plenteous flood,
For her heart supplied her eyes.

Oh, my Savior, oh, my Savior,
Where has my Savior gone?
Oh, my Savior, here’s my Savior,
He has risen from the tomb.
hymns.first_line: Mary to her Savior’s tomb
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 451 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Martin
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1738
stanzas:
Jesus, Lover of my soul,
Let me to Thy bosom fly,
While the nearer waters roll,
While the tempest still is high!
Hide me, Oh my Savior, hide,
Till the storm of life is past;
Safe into the haven guide;
Oh receive my soul at last.

Other refuge I have none,
Hangs my helpless soul on Thee:
Leave, ah! leave me not alone,
Still support and comfort me;
All my trust on Thee is stayed,
All my help from Thee I bring,
Cover my defenseless head
With the shadow of Thy wing.

Wilt Thou not regard my call?
Wilt Thou not accept my prayer?
Lo! I faint, I sing, I fall
Lo! on Thee I cast my care.
Reach me out Thy gracious Hand,
While I of Thy strength receive,
Hoping against hope I stand,
Dying, and behold I live!
hymns.first_line: Jesus, Lover of my soul,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 452 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Holly Springs
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709
stanzas:
There is a house not made with hands,
Eternal, and on high;
And here my spirit, waiting stands,
Till God shall bid it fly.
Chorus:

I long to see my friends again
And hear them sweetly say;
Come, weary dove, here is thy home,
Then fold thy wings and stay.

Shortly this prison of my clay
Must be dissolved and fall;
Then, Oh my soul, with joy obey
Thy heav’nly Father’s call.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: There is a house not made with hands,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 453 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Better Land
hymns.author: O. A. Parris, 1935
stanzas:
The road to glory seems so long,
And sorrows often take my song;
Chorus:

I’m going to a better land,
Where troubles are unknown.
All sorrows will be gone,
We’ll sing around the throne in sweet accord,
Adoring Jesus our dear Lord.

From Jesus’ side I will not stray,
I know he’ll guide me all the way.
(Chorus)

I know it is not very far
To heaven where my treasures are.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: The road to glory seems so long,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 454 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Soar Away
hymns.author: Collection of Hymns and Spiritual Songs, 1814
stanzas:
I want a sober mind,
An all sustaining eye,
To see my God above,
And to the heavens fly.
Chorus:

I’d soar away above the sky,
I’d fly to see my God above.

I want a Godly fear,
A quick discerning eye,
That looks to Thee my God,
And see the tempter fly.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: I want a sober mind,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 455 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sacred Mount
hymns.author: Philip Doddridge, 1755
stanzas:
Sing, Oh ye ransomed of the Lord,
Your great Redeemer sing.
Chorus:

Pilgrims for Zion’s city bound,
Be joyful in your King,
A hand divine shall lead you on,
Through all the blissful road,
Till to the sacred mount you rise,
And see your smiling God.

March on in your Redeemer’s strength,
Pursue His footsteps still.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Sing, Oh ye ransomed of the Lord,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 456 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Wayfaring Stranger
hymns.author: Bever’s Christian Songster, 1858
stanzas:
I am a poor, wayfaring stranger,
While journ’ying through this world of woe,
Yet, there’s no sickness, toil nor danger,
In that bright world to which I go.
I’m going there to see my Father,
I’m going there no more to roam;
Chorus:

I’m only going over Jordan,
I’m only going over home.

I know dark clouds will gather o’er me,
I know my way is rough and steep;
Yet beaut’ous fields lie just before me,
Where God’s redeemed their vigils keep.
I’m going there to see my Mother,
She said she’d meet me when I come.
(Chorus)
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: I am a poor, wayfaring stranger,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 457 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Friendship
hymns.author: John Newton, 1779
stanzas:
“Mercy, O Thou Son of David,”
Thus poor blind Bartimeus prayed,
“Others by Thy Word are saved,
Now to me afford Thine aid.”
Many for his crying chid him,
But he called the louder still,
Till the gracious Savior bid him,
“Come and ask me what you will.”
hymns.first_line: “Mercy, O Thou Son of David,”
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 458 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Tolling Bell
hymns.author: Mary Stanley Bunce Dana
stanzas:
Shed not a tear o’er your friend’s early bier,
When I am gone.
Smile when the slow tolling bell you shall hear,
When I am gone.
Weep not for me as you stand ’round my grave,
Think who has died His beloved to save,
Think of the crown all the ransomed shall wear,
When I am gone.
hymns.first_line: Shed not a tear o’er your friend’s early bier,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 459 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sardis
hymns.author: Charles’ Hymns and Spiritual Songs, 1803
stanzas:
Come on, my fellow pilgrims, come,
And let us all be hast’ning home,
We soon shall land on yon blest shore,
Where pains and sorrows are no more,
There we our Jesus shall adore
Forever blest.

No period then our joys shall know
Secure from ev’ry mortal foe;
No sickness there, no want or pain,
Shall e’er disturb our rest again,
When with Immanuel we reign,
Forever blest.
hymns.first_line: Come on, my fellow pilgrims, come,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 460 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Shining Star
hymns.author: Vs. 1 Nahum Tate, 1700 & Vs. 2 William Billings, 1786
stanzas:
While shepherds watched their flocks by night,
All seated on the ground,
The angel of the Lord came down,
And glory shone around.
On this day is born to you
A Savior meek and mild;
Haste ye all to Bethlehem
And kneel before the Child.

Lay down your crooks and quit your flocks,
To Bethlehem repair;
And let your wand’ring steps be spared,
By yonder shining star.
Seek ye not in palaces,
Nor regal curtains draw.
Search the stable, see your God
Extended on the straw.
hymns.first_line: While shepherds watched their flocks by night,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 461 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Faith and Hope
stanzas:
What shall I do, shall I lay down
And sink in deep despair?
Will He forever wear a frown
Nor hear my feeble prayer?
No, He will put His strength in me;
He knows the way I’ve strolled;
And when I’m tried sufficiently,
I shall come forth as gold.

When I can read my title clear
To mansions in the skies,
I’ll bid farewell to ev’ry fear,
And wipe my weeping eyes.
When we’ve been there ten thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun;
We’ve no less days to sing God’s praise
Than when we first begun.
hymns.first_line: What shall I do, shall I lay down
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 462 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Our Humble Faith
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Lord, how divine Thy comforts are,
How heav’nly is the place,
Where Jesus spreads the sacred feast
Of His redeeming grace.
Our humble faith is made to rise
While sitting ’round His throne,
And back to Calvary it flies
To view its groaning Lord.
hymns.first_line: Lord, how divine Thy comforts are,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 463 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sheppard
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
How beauteous are their feet
Who stand on Zion’s hill;
Who bring salvation on their tongues,
And words of peace reveal!

How charming is their voice;
How sweet the tidings are.
Zion, behold thy Savior King,
He reigns and triumphs here!
hymns.first_line: How beauteous are their feet
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 464 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Where There’s No Trouble and Sorrow
hymns.tune: Where There’s No Trouble and Sorrow
stanzas:
I have my troubles here below
As the narrow way I follow,
But there’s a land of peace and rest,
Where there’s no trouble or sorrow.
Yes, my loved ones are now over there,
And I know I soon will follow,
I’ll see my Savior in that land
Where there’s no trouble or sorrow.
hymns.first_line: I have my troubles here below
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 465 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Haynes Creek
hymns.author: Ingram Cobbin, 1843
stanzas:
A throne of grace, then let us go
And offer up our prayer;
A gracious God will mercy show
To all that worship there.
A throne of grace, oh, at that throne
Our knees have often bent,
And God has showered His blessing down
As oft, as often as we went.
hymns.first_line: A throne of grace, then let us go
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 466 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Lisbon
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Welcome, sweet day of rest,
That saw the Lord arise;
Welcome to this reviving breast
And these rejoicing eyes.

The King Himself comes near,
To feast His saints today;
Here we may sit and see Him here,
And love, and praise, and pray.
hymns.first_line: Welcome, sweet day of rest,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 467 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Bristol
hymns.author: Joseph Addison, 1712
stanzas:
The spacious firmament on high,
With all the blue, ethereal sky,
The spangled heav’ns, a shining frame,
Their great Original proclaim.
Th’unwearied sun, from day to day,
Does his Creator’s pow’r display,
And publishes to ev’ry land
The work of the almighty hand.
hymns.first_line: The spacious firmament on high,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 468 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Mercy Seat
hymns.author: Hugh Stowell, 1828
stanzas:
From ev’ry stormy wind that blows,
From ev’ry swelling tide of woes,
There is a calm, a sure retreat,
’Tis found beneath the mercy seat.
Chorus:

There is a place where Jesus sheds
The oil of gladness on our heads,
A place than all besides more sweet,
It is the blood-bought mercy seat.

There is a scene where spirits blend,
Where friends hold fellowship with friends,
Though sundered far, by faith they meet
Around one common mercy seat.
hymns.first_line: From ev’ry stormy wind that blows,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 470 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Savior’s Name
hymns.author: Frederick Whitfield, 1855
stanzas:
There is a name I love to hear,
I love to sing its worth;
It sounds like music to mine ear,
The sweetest name on earth.

It bids my trembling soul rejoice,
And dries each rising tear;
It tells me in a small still voice
To trust and not to fear.
hymns.first_line: There is a name I love to hear,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 471 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Akin
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Within Thy circling pow’r I stand,
On ev’ry side I find Thy hand;
Awake, asleep, at home, abroad,
I am surrounded still with God.
hymns.first_line: Within Thy circling pow’r I stand,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 472 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Carmarthen
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1741
stanzas:
Rejoice! the Lord is King:
Your Lord and King adore!
Mortals, give thanks and sing,
And triumph evermore:
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice!
Rejoice, again I say, rejoice!

Rejoice in glorious hope!
Jesus the Judge shall come
And take His servants up
To their eternal home:
We soon shall hear the angel’s voice,
The trump of God shall sound, rejoice!
hymns.first_line: Rejoice! the Lord is King:
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 473 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Mount Desert
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Unshaken as the sacred hill,
And firm as mountains be,
Firm as a rock the soul shall rest,
That leans, Oh Lord, on Thee.

Not walls or hills could guard so well
Old Salem’s happy ground,
As those eternal arms of love
That ev’ry saint surround.
hymns.first_line: Unshaken as the sacred hill,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 474 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: A Thankful Heart
hymns.author: Anne Steele, 1760
stanzas:
Give me a calm, a thankful heart
From ev’ry murmur free;
The blessing of Thy grace impart,
And make me live to Thee.

Let the sweet hope that Thou art mine
My life and death attend;
Thy presence through my journey shine,
And crown my journey’s end.
hymns.first_line: Give me a calm, a thankful heart
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 475 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Throne of Grace
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1721
stanzas:
Oh, that I knew the secret place,
Where I might find my God,
I’d spread my want before His face,
And pour my woes abroad.
Arise, my soul, from deep distress,
And banish ev’ry fear,
He calls thee to His throne of grace,
To spread thy sorrows there.
hymns.first_line: Oh, that I knew the secret place,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 476 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Lord, We Adore Thee
hymns.author: Owel W. Denson, 1960
stanzas:
Holy Lord, we worship Thee,
Thine are we eternally,
Yielded in Thy presence bow,
Let us share Thy favor now.
Chorus:

Holy Lord, holy Lord,
We have met in sweet accord;
As we bow before Thy shrine,
Make us, Savior, wholly Thine.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Holy Lord, we worship Thee,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 477 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: My Rising Sun
hymns.author: William Cowper, 1774
stanzas:
God moves in a mysterious way
His wonders to perform;
He plants His footsteps in the sea
And rides upon the storm.
In darkest night when he appears,
My sorrows will be gone,
He is my soul’s sweet morning star
And he’s my rising sun.

He forms the sinful man anew,
Subdues the love of sin;
He takes away the heart of stone
And plants His grace within.
He came from heav’n our souls to save,
Applies redeeming blood,
Bids all our guilt and fears removed,
Leaves us at peace with God.
hymns.first_line: God moves in a mysterious way
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 478 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Chester
hymns.author: Philip Doddridge, 1755
stanzas:
Let the high heav’ns your songs invite,
These spacious fields of brilliant light,
Where sun and moon and planets roll,
And stars that glow from pole to pole.

Sun, moon, and stars convey Thy praise,
’Round the whole earth and never stand,
So when Thy truth began its race,
It touched and glanced on ev’ry hand.
hymns.first_line: Let the high heav’ns your songs invite,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 479 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Redemption
hymns.author: John T. Hocutt, 1959
stanzas:
There upon the cross of Calvary
Our blessed Savior died;
There between two thieves our blessed Lord
For us was crucified.
Chorus:

Oh, His blood was shed that we might live
With Him when life is o’er,
And upon the clouds of glory ride
Safe to that peaceful shore.

Oh! He suffered there for guilty man,
His life so freely gave,
When He paid the debt we could not pay
And triumphed o’er the grave.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: There upon the cross of Calvary
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 480 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Novakoski
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Come, we who love the Lord,
And let our joys be known;
Join in a song with sweet accord,
And thus surround the throne.

Let those refuse to sing
Who never knew our God;
But children of the heav’nly King
May speak their joys abroad.

Then let our songs abound,
And ev’ry tear be dry;
We’re marching through Immanuel’s ground
To fairer worlds on high.
hymns.first_line: Come, we who love the Lord,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 481 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Mulberry Grove
hymns.author: H. Wood, 1869 & Vs. 2 A. M. Cagle, 1966
stanzas:
My sands of life are running fast,
I can’t recall one moment past;
I’ve much to do in little space,
Oh can I yet be saved by grace?
Oh can I yet one effort make?
hymns.first_line: My sands of life are running fast,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 482 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Eternal Light
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
I’m not ashamed to own my Lord,
Or to defend His cause,
Maintain the honor of His Word,
The glory of His cross.
Jesus, my God, I know His name,
His name is all my trust,
Nor will He put my soul to shame,
Nor let my hope be lost.

Firm as His throne His promise stands
And He can well secure
What I’ve committed to His hands
Till the decisive hour.
Then He will own my worthless name
Before His Father’s face,
And in the new Jerusalem
Appoint my soul a place.
hymns.first_line: I’m not ashamed to own my Lord,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 483 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Heavenly Union
stanzas:
Come, saints and sinners, hear me tell
The wonders of Emmanuel,
Who saved me from a burning hell,
And brought my soul with Christ to dwell,
And gave me heav’nly union.

When Jesus saw me from on high,
Beheld my soul in ruin lie,
He looked on me with pitying eye,
And said to me as He passed by,
“With God you have no union.”

But when depressed and lost in sin,
My dear Redeemer took me in,
And with His blood He washed me clean,
And Oh what seasons I have seen,
Since first I felt this union!
hymns.first_line: Come, saints and sinners, hear me tell
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 484 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Agatite
hymns.author: Edward Perronet, 1779
stanzas:
All hail the pow’r of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall;
Chorus:

Bring forth the royal diadem,
And crown Him Lord of all.

His mercy and His righteousness
Let heav’n and earth proclaim;
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: All hail the pow’r of Jesus’ name,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 485 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Beneficence
hymns.author: Tate & Brady’s New Version, 1696
stanzas:
That man is blessed who stands in awe
Of God and loves His sacred law.
His seed on earth shall be renowned
And with successive honors crowned.
His house a seat of wealth shall be,
An unexhausted treasury,
His justice free from all decay,
His blessings to His heirs convey.
hymns.first_line: That man is blessed who stands in awe
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 486 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Soldier’s Delight
hymns.author: C. O. Woodard, 1918
stanzas:
While in the army I remain,
I’ll speak the truth and bear the blame,
And when on board the ship I am,
I’ll sing my Savior’s praise the same.

Oh, if your captain calls for you,
Put on your armor bold and true,
Put forth your strength, put forth your rod,
Fight for your country and your God.
hymns.first_line: While in the army I remain,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 487 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: As We Go On
hymns.author: O. H. Handley, 1959
stanzas:
Now, let our works and virtue show,
To prove our faith as on we go,
Religion bears our spirits up,
While we expect that blessed hope.
We get the blessings of the Lord,
And we expect the great reward.
Most precious is Thy love, Oh Lord,
It guides us as we go along
To join that great celestial band,
To sing Thy praise forevermore.
hymns.first_line: Now, let our works and virtue show,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 488 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Savior’s Call
hymns.author: Lyra Catholica, 1851
stanzas:
Come, wand’ring sheep, oh, come!
I’ll bind thee to my breast,
I’ll bear thee to my home,
And lay thee down to rest.

I saw thee stray forlorn,
And heard thee faintly cry,
And on the tree of scorn,
For thee I deign to die.

I shield thee from alarms,
And wilt thou not be blest?
I bear thee in my arms;
Thou bear me in thy breast.
hymns.first_line: Come, wand’ring sheep, oh, come!
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 489 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: My Shepherd Guides
hymns.author: Era Tidwell Godsey, 1959
stanzas:
The Lord my precious Shepherd is,
He guides me day by day,
If I but trust His holy word,
In paths of right I’ll stay.
I’ll fear no evil if He leads,
Beside the waters still,
He anoints my head with oil so sweet,
My cup with joy He fills.

Though I walk through the valley dark,
No shadows will befall,
Thy rod, Thy staff, they comfort me,
Thou art my God, my all.
Surely Thy goodness and Thy love,
Thy mercy free on call,
Will keep me safe from sin and strife,
I’ll praise Thee, Lord of all.
hymns.first_line: The Lord my precious Shepherd is,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 490 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Oh, What Love
hymns.author: Eula Denson Johnson, 1960
stanzas:
Jesus left His home on high,
Oh, what love, what wondrous love!
And for sinners came to die, what love.
Bled and died on Calvary,
All because of you and me,
Oh, what love, what wonderful love.
It was love He had for me,
Caused by my blinded eyes to see,
Oh, what love, what wondrous love!

Happiness and joy I’ve found,
For I’m on much higher ground,
You can share along the way of love.
For my Savior made the way,
Leading to a brighter day,
Oh, what love, oh, yes, what wondrous love.
I can shout, and I can sing,
Make His praises gladly ring,
Oh, what love, what wondrous love!
hymns.first_line: Jesus left His home on high,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 491 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Invocation (Second)
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707, Alt.
hymns.first_line: Arise, my soul, my joyful pow’rs,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 492 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Amanda Ray
hymns.author: Frances R. Havergal, 1878
stanzas:
I know I love Thee better, Lord,
Than any earthly joy;
For Thou hast given me sweet peace,
That nothing can destroy.

Oh Savior, precious Savior mine,
What will the future be;
If such a life of joy can crown
Our walk on earth with Thee?
hymns.first_line: I know I love Thee better, Lord,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 493 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Big Creek
stanzas:
Weary soldiers of the cross, seek rest
With the Savior as your guide;
Lay your head upon His heav’nly breast,
And in peace e’ermore abide.

In that last sad hour, ’mid friends so dear,
Death your trembling soul will free;
And a father’s loving voice you’ll hear,
Saying, “Wand’rer, come to me.”
hymns.first_line: Weary soldiers of the cross, seek rest
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 494 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Midnight Cry
hymns.author: Baptist Harmony, 1834
stanzas:
When the midnight cry began,
Oh what lamentation,
Thousands sleeping in their sins,
Neglecting their salvation.
Lo, the Bridegroom is at hand,
Who will kindly treat Him?
Surely all the waiting band
Will now go forth to meet Him.

Some, indeed, did wait awhile,
Shone without a rival,
But they spent their seeming oil,
Long since last revival.
Many souls who thought they’d light,
Oh, when the scene was closed,
Now against the Bridegroom fight,
And so they stand opposed.
hymns.first_line: When the midnight cry began,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 495 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Rock That is Higher Than I
hymns.author: Dobell’s Selection, 1810
hymns.tune: The Rock That is Higher Than I
stanzas:
Convinced as a sinner, to Jesus I come,
Informed by the gospel for such there is room;
O’erwhelmed with sorrows for sin I will cry,
Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
Chorus:
Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

When sorely afflicted and ready to faint,
Before my Redeemer I’ll spread my complaint;
’Mid storms and distresses my soul shall rely
On Jesus, the rock that is higher than I.
(Chorus)

’Tis there with the chosen of Jesus,
I long to dwell and eternally join in the song,
And praising and blessings, with angels on high,
It’s Jesus, the rock that is higher than I.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Convinced as a sinner, to Jesus I come,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 496 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Natick
hymns.author: Edward W. Billups, 1854
stanzas:
Bleeding hearts defiled by sin,
Jesus Christ can make you clean;
Contrite souls with guilt oppressed,
Jesus Christ can give you rest.
Chorus:

Sweet Redeemer from above,
Borne on wings of love.

You that mourn our follies past,
Precious hours and years laid waste,
Turn to God, Oh turn and live,
Jesus Christ can still forgive.
(Chorus)

Fainting souls in peril’s hour,
Yield not to the Tempter’s pow’r
On the risen Lord rely,
Jesus Christ now reigns on high.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Bleeding hearts defiled by sin,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 497 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Resurrection Day
stanzas:
Oh, Resurrection Day!
When Christ the Savior comes some morning fair,
The grave will open wide
And saints will rise to meet Him in the air.
Chorus:

Oh! May we meet in heav’n
To sing the praises of our Lord and King,
And gathered ’round the snow-white throne
Make heaven’s portals ring.
hymns.first_line: Oh, Resurrection Day!
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 498 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: At Rest
hymns.author: James Montgomery, 1825 & Vs. 3 Floyd M. Frederick, 1960
stanzas:
The world can never give
The bliss for which we sigh;
’Tis not the whole of life to live,
Nor all of death to die.

Beyond this vale of tears
There is a life above,
Unmeasured by the flight of years,
An endless life of love.

Farewell, dear friends, farewell,
For just a little while;
We’ll meet and sing on heaven’s shore,
Where parting comes no more.
hymns.first_line: The world can never give
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 499 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Living Hope
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Blest be the everlasting God,
The Father of our Lord;
Be His abounding mercy praised,
His majesty adored.
Chorus:

When from the dead He raised His Son
And called Him to the sky,
He gave our souls a living hope
That they should never die.

Saints by the pow’r of God are kept,
Till the salvation come;
We walk by faith as strangers here,
Till Christ shall call us home.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Blest be the everlasting God,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 500 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: O’Leary
hymns.author: Philip Doddridge, 1755
stanzas:
And will the Judge descend,
And must the dead arise;
And not a single soul escape
His all-discerning eyes?

How will my heart endure
The terrors of that day,
When earth and heav’n before His face
Astonished shrink away?

But ere the trumpet shakes
The mansions of the dead,
Hark, from the gospel’s cheering sound,
What joyful tidings spread.
hymns.first_line: And will the Judge descend,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 501 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: A Charge to Keep
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1762
stanzas:
A charge to keep I have,
A God to glorify,
A never-dying soul to save,
And fit it for the sky.
To serve the present age,
My calling to fulfill,
Oh may it all my pow’rs engage
To do my Master’s will.

Arm me with jealous care,
As in Thy sight to live;
And Oh Thy servant, Lord, prepare,
A strict account to give.
Help me watch and pray,
And on Thyself rely,
Assured, if I my trust betray,
I shall forever die.
hymns.first_line: A charge to keep I have,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 502 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Lloyd
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
My Savior and my King,
Thy beauties are divine;
Thy lips with blessing overflow,
And ev’ry grace is Thine.

The smilings of Thy face,
How amiable they are;
’Tis heav’n to rest in Thine embrace,
And nowhere else but there.

Nor earth, nor all the sky,
Can one delight afford;
No, not a drop of Thy real joy,
Without Thy presence, Lord.
hymns.first_line: My Savior and my King,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 503 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Wood Street
hymns.author: Tate & Brady’s New Version, 1696
stanzas:
When we our wearied limbs to rest
Sat down by proud Euphrates’ stream:
We wept with doleful thoughts oppressed,
And Zion was our mournful theme.

Our harps that when with joy we sung
Were wont their tuneful parts to bear,
With silent strings neglected hung,
On willow trees that withered there.
hymns.first_line: When we our wearied limbs to rest
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 504 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Where Ceaseless Ages Roll
stanzas:
Come, on, my friends, and go with me,
For I am on my journey home.
My Savior welcomes you with me
To live where joys are ever known.
Chorus:

Come, go with me to that fair land
Where ceaseless ages roll.
hymns.first_line: Come, on, my friends, and go with me,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 505 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Ark
hymns.author: Mercer’s Cluster, 1829
stanzas:
When Noah with his favored few
Was ordered to embark,
Eight human souls, a little crew,
Entered on his ark.
Chorus:
hymns.first_line: When Noah with his favored few
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 506 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sermon on the Mount
hymns.author: Holy Bible: Matthew 5
stanzas:
And seeing the multitudes,
He went up into a mount;
And when He was set,
His disciples came unto Him.
He opened His mouth,
There blessings poured out
To the children about
And none were left out.

Blessed are the pure in heart,
For they shall see the kingdom of heav’n.

The meek He blessed with righteousness,
The weak, the dumb, the blind ones too,
Will sing to His praise when we all reach home.
hymns.first_line: And seeing the multitudes,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 507 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Corley
hymns.author: Marcus M. Wells, 1858
hymns.composer: John Wilson, 17th century & Arr. Richard L. DeLong, 1988
stanzas: Chorus:

Weary souls fore’er rejoice
While they hear that sweetest voice
Whisper softly, “Follow me,
I’ll guide thee home.”

Ever present, truest friend,
Ever near Thine aid to lend,
Leave us not to doubt and fear,
Groping on in darkness drear;
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Holy Spirit, faithful guide,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 510 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Great Redeemer
hymns.author: Anne Steele, 1760
stanzas:
Look up, my soul, with cheerful eyes,
See where the great Redeemer lives,
I’ll build an altar to His name,
And to the world proclaim His grace.
hymns.first_line: Look up, my soul, with cheerful eyes,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 511 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Spirit Shall Return
hymns.author: Holy Bible: Ecclesiastes
stanzas:
When the sun, or the light,
Or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened,
Or the clouds return after the rain,
Or the silver cord be loosed,
Then shall the dust return
To the earth as it was,
And the spirit shall return
To God who gave it.
hymns.first_line: When the sun, or the light,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 512 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Joyful
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1724
stanzas:
Am I a soldier of the cross,
A foll’wer of the Lamb?
And shall I fear to own His cause,
Or blush to speak His name?
Must I be carried to the skies
On flow’ry beds of ease,
While others fought to win the prize
And sailed through bloody seas?
Chorus:

Oh, that will be joyful to meet
To part no more
On Canaan’s happy shore;
We all shall meet at Jesus’ feet
With those who’ve gone before.

Are there no foes for me to face?
Must I not stem the flood?
Is this vile world a friend to grace
To help me on to God?
Sure I must fight if I would reign;
Increase my courage, Lord;
I’ll bear the toil, endure the pain,
Supported by Thy Word.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: Am I a soldier of the cross,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 513 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Federal Street
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709
stanzas:
My dear Redeemer and my Lord,
I read my duty in Thy Word;
But in Thy life the law appears,
Drawn out in living characters.

Such was Thy truth and such Thy zeal,
Such def’rence to Thy Father’s will;
Such love and meekness so divine,
I would transcribe and make them mine.

Cold mountains and the midnight air
Witnessed the fervor of Thy prayer;
The desert Thy temptations knew,
Thy conflict and Thy vict’ry, too.

Be Thou my pattern; make me bear
More of Thy gracious image here;
Then God, the Judge, shall own my name,
Among the foll’wers of the Lamb.
hymns.first_line: My dear Redeemer and my Lord,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 515 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: DeLong
hymns.author: John Blain, 1834
stanzas:
And now, my friends, both old and young,
I hope in Christ you’ll still go on;
And if on earth we meet no more,
Oh may we meet on Canaan’s shore.
I hope you’ll all remember me
If you on earth no more I see;
An int’rest in your prayers I crave,
That we may meet beyond the grave.

How oft I’ve seen your flowing tears
And heard you tell your hopes and fears;
Your hearts with love were seen to flame,
Which makes me hope we’ll meet again.
Ye mourning souls, lift up your eyes
To glorious mansions in the skies;
Oh trust His grace — in Canaan’s land
We’ll no more take the parting hand.

Oh glorious day, Oh blessed hope!
My soul leaps forward at the thought;
When on that happy, happy land,
We’ll no more take the parting hand.
But with our blessed holy Lord,
We’ll shout and sing with one accord.
And there we’ll all with Jesus dwell,
So loving Christians, fare you well!
hymns.first_line: And now, my friends, both old and young,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 516 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Mars Hill
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
How shall the young secure their hearts
And guard their lives from sin?
Thy Word the choicest rule imparts,
To keep the conscience clean.

The Word is everlasting truth,
How pure is ev’ry page!
That holy book shall guide our youth,
And well support our age.
hymns.first_line: How shall the young secure their hearts
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 517 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Heavenly Anthem
hymns.author: Holy Bible: Psalm 19:1-4, 7-8, 11, 14
stanzas:
The heavens declare the glory of God;
The firmament showeth His handiwork,
Day unto day utt’reth speech,
Night unto night showeth knowledge,
There is no speech nor language
Where their voice is not heard,
Their line is gone through all the earth,
And their words to the end of the world.
The law of the Lord is perfect,
Converting the soul,
The testimony of the Lord is sure,
Making the wise simple,
The statues of the Lord are right,
Rejoicing the heart:
The commandment of the Lord is pure,
Enlightening the eyes.
Moreover, by them is Thy servant warned.
Let the words of my mouth
And the meditations of my heart
Be acceptable in Thy sight, Oh Lord,
My strength and my Redeemer.
hymns.first_line: The heavens declare the glory of God;
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 518 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Parting Friends (Third)
hymns.author: Primitive Hymns, 1858
hymns.first_line: Our cheerful voices let us raise,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 521 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Ye Heedless Ones
hymns.author: New England Sunday School Hymn Book, 1830
stanzas:
Ye heedless ones who wildly stroll,
The grave will soon become your bed,
Where silence reigns and vapors roll
In solemn darkness ’round your head.
Your friends will pass the lonesome place
And with a sigh move slowly on
Still gazing on the spires of grass,
With which your graves are overgrown.
hymns.first_line: Ye heedless ones who wildly stroll,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 522 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Pleyel’s Hymn (Second)
hymns.author: John Newton, 1779
stanzas:
Sinner, art thou still secure?
Wilt thou still refuse to pray?
Can thy heart or hands endure
In the Lord’s avenging day?

Lord, prepare us by Thy grace,
Soon we must resign our breath,
And our souls be called to pass,
Through the iron gate of death.
hymns.first_line: Sinner, art thou still secure?
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 523 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Twenty-Third Psalm
hymns.author: Holy Bible: Psalm 23
hymns.first_line: The Lord is my Shepherd;
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 524 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: My Life and Breath
hymns.author: Samuel Stennett, 1787
stanzas:
He saw me sinking in distress,
And flew to my relief,
For me He bore the shameful cross,
And carried all my grief.
Chorus:

To Him I owe my life and breath
And all the joys I have,
He makes me triumph over death,
And saves me from the grave.

To heav’n the place of His abode,
He brings my weary feet;
Shows me the glories of my God,
And makes my joys complete.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: He saw me sinking in distress,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 527 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Showers of Blessings
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
hymns.composer: Joseph Stone, 1793 & Arr. A. A. Blocker, 1959
stanzas:
With songs and honors sounding loud,
Address the Lord on high,
Over the heav’ns He spreads His clouds,
And waters veil the sky.
He sends His show’rs of blessing down
To cheer the plains below;
He makes the grass the mountains crown;
And corn in valleys grow.
hymns.first_line: With songs and honors sounding loud,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 528 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: A Glad New Song
hymns.author: Jonathan B. Atchinson, 1891
stanzas:
I’ve learned to sing a glad, new song,
Of praise unto our King!
And now with all my ransomed pow’rs
His praises I will sing.
I’ve learned to sing the song of peace,
’Tis sweeter ev’ry day,
Since Jesus calmed my troubled soul,
And bore my sins away.

I’ve learned to sing the song of joy,
My cup is running o’er
With blessings full of peace and love,
And still there’s more and more.
Soon I shall sing the glad, new song,
Of Moses and the Lamb,
With all the sainted hosts above,
Before the great I Am.
hymns.first_line: I’ve learned to sing a glad, new song,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 530 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Dura
hymns.author: Dura Ann Campbell Blackmon
stanzas:
Dear Lord, forgive my sins, I pray,
And lead me in the narrow way,
Oh Lord, give me strength by day,
Have mercy, Lord, for this I pray.
hymns.first_line: Dear Lord, forgive my sins, I pray,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 531 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Peace and Joy
hymns.author: John Bowring, 1825
stanzas:
In the cross of Christ I glory,
Tow’ring o’er the wrecks of time;
All the light of sacred story,
Gathers ’round its head sublime.
When the woes of life o’ertake me,
Hopes deceive and fears annoy;
Never shall the cross forsake me,
Lo! it glows with peace and joy.

When the sun of bliss is beaming
Light and love upon my way;
From the cross the radiance streaming
Adds more luster to the day.
Bane and blessing, pain and pleasure,
By the cross are satisfied;
Peace is there that knows no measure,
Joys that from all time abide.
hymns.first_line: In the cross of Christ I glory,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 532 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: New Georgia
stanzas:
The mighty hand of God doth reign,
As in the ages past;
His blood has entered death’s domain
To guide us home at last.
His praise we’ll sing the earth around,
And upward lift our eyes
While slumb’ring tenants of the ground
In living armies rise.

When sun and moon, and earth, and stars,
And time shall be no more,
Through His own blood and battle scars,
We’ll land on Canaan’s shore.
His praise forever we shall sing,
And mount the upper sky;
And to the palace of our king
On wings of love we’ll fly.
hymns.first_line: The mighty hand of God doth reign,
