hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 534 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Shawmut
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1759
stanzas:
Oh that I could repent!
With all my idols part,
And to Thy gracious eye present,
A humble contrite heart.

A heart with grief oppressed,
For having grieved my God;
A troubled heart that cannot rest,
Till sprinkled with Thy blood.

Jesus on me bestow
The penitent desire:
With true sincerity of woe
My aching breast inspire.

With soft’ning pity look,
And melt my hardness down;
Strike the love’s resistless stroke,
And break this heart of stone.
hymns.first_line: Oh that I could repent!
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 535 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sweet Majesty
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Oh, the delights, the heav’nly joys,
The glories of the place,
Where Jesus sheds the brightest beams,
Of His o’erflowing grace.
Sweet majesty and awful love
Sit smiling on His brow,
And all the glorious ranks above,
At humble distance bow.
hymns.first_line: Oh, the delights, the heav’nly joys,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 536 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Hampton
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Speak of the wonders of that love
Which Gabriel plays on ev’ry chord;
From all below, and all above,
Loud hallelujahs to the Lord.
hymns.first_line: Ye flow’ry plains, proclaim His skill;
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 538 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Supplication
hymns.author: E. Foy Frederick, 1959
stanzas:
Glory to Thee, my God on high,
For all the blessings of this life;
Oh, let Thy mercy fill my heart,
And let all fears from me depart.

Oh, let Thy thought and praise arise
In grateful anthems in the skies;
Take Thou my soul when life is o’er,
To live with Thee forever more.
hymns.first_line: Glory to Thee, my God on high,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 539 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Nidrah
hymns.author: Samuel Stennett, 1787
stanzas:
How charming is the place
Where my Redeemer God
Unveils the beauties of His face
And sheds His love abroad.
Give me, Oh Lord, a place
Within Thy blest abode,
Among the children of Thy grace,
The servants of my God.
hymns.first_line: How charming is the place
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 540 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Home of the Blest
hymns.author: Missionary Minstrel, 1826
stanzas:
Why should our tears in sorrow flow
When God recalls His own,
And bids them leave a world of woe
For an eternal home?
Their toils are past, their work is done,
And they are fully blest,
They fought the fight, the vict’ry won,
And entered into rest.
hymns.first_line: Why should our tears in sorrow flow
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 541 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: I’ll Seek His Blessings
stanzas:
My hope is in the Lord,
The blessed, bleeding Lamb,
I’ll seek His blessings ev’ry noon,
And pay my vows at night.
hymns.first_line: My hope is in the Lord,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 542 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Thou Art God
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting Thou art God,
Through endless years the same.

Under the shadow of Thy throne,
Still may we dwell secure,
Sufficient is Thine arm alone,
And our defense is sure.
hymns.first_line: Before the hills in order stood,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 543 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Praise Him
stanzas:
I’ll praise Him while He gives me breath,
I long to praise Him after death.
I’ll praise Him when I’m called to die,
And shout salvation when I die.

Time soon shall stop my fleeting breath,
And in His arms resigned to death,
My trembling soul to all can tell
That Jesus doeth all things well.

Then I shall see Him face to face,
And praise Him in that holy place.
My theme Through all eternity
Shall glory, glory, glory be.
hymns.first_line: I’ll praise Him while He gives me breath,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 544 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Pilgrim’s Way
stanzas:
Dark and thorny is the desert,
Through which pilgrims make their way.
But beyond this vale of sorrow
Is a land of perfect day.
Tired and thirsty are the pilgrims
As they cross the burning sand,
But the Master walks beside them
Till they reach the heav’nly land.
hymns.first_line: Dark and thorny is the desert,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 545 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: My Brightest Days
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
My God, the spring of all my joys,
The life of my delights,
The glory of my brightest days,
And comfort of my nights.

In darkest shades if He appears,
My dawning is begun,
He is my soul’s sweet morning star,
And He’s my rising sun.
hymns.first_line: My God, the spring of all my joys,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 546 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Granville
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Remember, Lord, our mortal state;
How frail our lives! how short the date!
Where is the man that draws his breath,
Safe from disease, secure from death?

Lord, while we see whole nations die,
Our flesh and sense repine and cry;
Must death forever rage and reign?
Or hast Thou made mankind in vain?
hymns.first_line: Remember, Lord, our mortal state;
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 547 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Wootten
hymns.author: Hugh McGraw, 1976
stanzas:
I soon shall view the promised land,
I soon shall sing with the angels’ band,
For Jesus’ blood has made me free;
And I soon shall sing in eternity.
I want to live for Jesus ev’ry day,
I want to sing His praises once again,
I want to feel that He is ever near,
To guard and guide my weary soul
To that eternal world of joy.
hymns.first_line: I soon shall view the promised land,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 548 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Phillips Farewell
hymns.author: George Phillips, 1962
stanzas:
It is one thing I surely know,
It is to heav’n I want to go
To sing His praise where angels sing,
To praise my Lord and Savior King.

My life has been to sing God’s praise
In hope of the eternal days;
I mean to do the best I can
And meet you in the promised land.

My friends have been so good to me,
And where you go I want to be;
My love for you no tongue can tell,
Dear loving friends, so fare you well.
hymns.first_line: My days on earth are almost gone,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 549 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Blissful Dawning
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
My God, the spring of all my joys,
The life of my delight,
The glory of my brightest days,
And comfort of my nights.
In darkest shades if Thou appear,
My blissful dawning is begun,
Thou art my soul’s bright morning star,
And Thou my rising sun.
hymns.first_line: My God, the spring of all my joys,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 550 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Jacob’s Vision
hymns.author: Hymns, Evangelical Association, 1850
stanzas:
As Jacob with travel was weary one day,
And at night on a stone for a pillow he lay,
There he saw in a vision a ladder so high,
That its foot was on earth and its top in the sky.
Chorus:

Alleluia to Jesus who died on the tree,
And hath raised up a ladder of mercy for me.

The ladder is long, it is strong and well-made,
It stood hundreds of years, and is not yet decayed;
Many millions have climbed it and reached Zion’s hill,
And thousands by faith are now climbing it still.
(Chorus)

Come, let us ascend! All may climb it who will,
For the angels of Jacob are guarding it still.
There are regions of light, there are mansions of bliss,
Oh, then, who would not climb such a ladder as this?
hymns.first_line: As Jacob with travel was weary one day,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 551 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Anthem on the Beginning
hymns.author: Holy Bible: John 1:1-10
stanzas:
In the beginning was the Word,
And the Word was with God,
And the Word was God,
The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made by Him,
And without Him was not anything made
That was made.
In Him was life; and the life was the light of men,
And the light shineth in darkness,
And the darkness comprehendeth it not.
There was a man sent from God,
Whose name was John,
Who came to bear witness of that light,
That all men through Him might believe.
John was not that Light,
But was sent to bear witness of that light,
The true light that cometh into the world,
And the world was made by Him.
hymns.first_line: In the beginning was the Word,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 553 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Portland
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
stanzas:
Sweet is the day of sacred rest,
No mortal cares shall seize my breast;
Oh, may my heart in tune be found,
Like David’s harp of solemn sound.

Then shall I see, and hear and know,
All I desired and wished below;
And ev’ry pow’r find sweet employ
In that eternal world of joy.
hymns.first_line: Sweet is the day of sacred rest,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 556 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Living Streams
hymns.author: Robertson’s Psalter, 1872
stanzas:
My Shepherd is the Lord most high,
And all my wants He will supply,
In pastures green he makes me lie,
And leads by streams that never die.

He in His mercy doth restore,
My soul when sinking in distress,
For His name’s sake He evermore
Leads me in paths of righteousness.

Yea, though I walk through death’s dark vale,
E’en there no evil shall I fear,
Because Thy presence shall not fail.
Thy rod and staff my soul shall cheer.

For me a table Thou hast spread
Before the faces of my foes;
With oil Thou dost anoint my head,
My cup is full and overflows.
hymns.first_line: My Shepherd is the Lord most high,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 558 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: My Home (Second)
hymns.author: Anonymous
stanzas:
We are told there is a home
In a land beyond the sky,
I hope to reach that happy place
Where the soul never dies,
And when my blessed Savior bids me come,
Then I shall live in heav’n above,
And see my Savior’s face.
I’ll thank Him for His Son
And Praise His saving grace,
And wonders of His love.
hymns.first_line: We are told there is a home
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 560 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Infinite Delight
stanzas:
Oh may our humble spirits stand
Among them clothed in white.
The lowest place at His right hand
Is infinite delight.
How will our joy and wonder rise,
When our returning King
Shall bear us homeward through the skies
On love’s triumphant wing.

Behold, what heav’nly prophets sang
Is now at last fulfilled,
That death should yield his ancient reign
And vanquish quite the field.
Let faith exalt her joyful voice,
And thus begin to sing,
Oh grave, where is thy triumph now,
And where, Oh death, thy sting?
hymns.first_line: Oh may our humble spirits stand
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 562 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Zion
stanzas:
While trav’ling down life’s weary road
Of troubles and despair,
We sometimes long for peace and joy
That waits God’s children there.
No pain nor death will we see there
On that delightful shore,
But all will be peace, joy, and love
With Christ forevermore.
hymns.first_line: While trav’ling down life’s weary road
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 564 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Hill of Zion
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
The hill of Zion yields,
A thousand sacred sweets,
Before we reach the heav’nly fields,
Or walk the golden streets.

Then let our songs abound,
And ev’ry tear be dry;
We’re marching through Immanuel’s ground,
To fairer worlds on high.
hymns.first_line: The hill of Zion yields,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 565 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Hebron
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707
stanzas:
Thus far the Lord hath led me on,
Thus far His pow’r prolonged my days;
And ev’ry ev’ning shall make known
Some fresh memorials of His grace.

Much of my time has run to waste,
And I, perhaps, am near my home.
But He forgives my follies past,
And gives me strength for days to come.

I lay my body down to sleep,
Peace is the pillow for my head;
While well-appointed angels keep
Their watchful stations ’round my bed.
hymns.first_line: Thus far the Lord hath led me on,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 566 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Great Day
stanzas:
I’ve a long time heard that there will be a judgment,
That there will be a judgment in that day.
Oh, sinner, where will you stand in that day?

I’ve a long time heard that the sun will be darkened,
That the sun will be darkened in that day.
Oh, sinner, where will you stand in that day?

I’ve a long time heard that the earth will be burning,
That the earth will be burning in that day.
Oh, sinner, where will you stand in that day?
hymns.first_line: I’ve a long time heard that there will be a judgment,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 567 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: I Want to Go to Heaven
hymns.tune: I Want to Go to Heaven
stanzas:
I want to go to heav’n, I do,
I want to see His face,
I want to hear Him sweetly say,
Come dwell with me at home.
Chorus:

I’m going home to be with Him,
To live through endless days,
And there with saints and angels join,
In hymns of joyful praise.

I want to work each day I live,
And do my Master’s will,
A life of faithful service give,
My mission to fulfill.
(Chorus)
hymns.first_line: I want to go to heav’n, I do,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 568 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Emmaus
hymns.author: Anne Steele, 1760
stanzas:
Dear Lord, what heav’nly wonders dwell
In Thy atoning blood;
By this are sinners snatched from hell
And rebels brought to God.

Oh may the sweet, the blissful theme
Fill ev’ry heart and tongue;
Till strangers love Thy charming name,
And join the sacred song.
hymns.first_line: Dear Lord, what heav’nly wonders dwell
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 569t (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Sacred Throne
hymns.author: John Kent, 1835
stanzas:
Beneath the sacred throne of God
I saw a river rise;
The streams where peace and pard’ning blood
Descended from the skies.

I stood amazed and wondered when
Or why this ocean rose;
That wafts salvation down to man,
His traitors and His foes.

That sacred flood from Jesus’ veins
Was free to make away;
And Mary’s or Manasseh’s stains,
Or sins more vile than they.
hymns.first_line: Beneath the sacred throne of God
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 569b (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Farewell to All (Second)
hymns.author: B. Hicks, 1832
stanzas:
The time is swiftly rolling on
When I must faint and die;
My body to the dust return,
And there forgotten lie.
My little children, near my heart,
And nature seems to bind;
It grieves me sorely to depart
And leave you all behind.

Let persecution rage around,
And antichrist appear,
My silent dust beneath the ground,
There’s no disturbance there.
Though I can never come to thee;
Let not this grieve your heart;
For you will shortly come to me,
Where we shall never part.
hymns.first_line: The time is swiftly rolling on
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 570 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Penitence
hymns.author: Joseph Swain
stanzas:
Oh, why should I wander a stranger from Thee,
Or cry in the desert for bread?
My foes will rejoice all my sorrows to see,
And smile at the tears I have shed.
Ye daughters of Zion, declare, have you seen
The star that on Israel shone?
Say, if in your tents my beloved has been,
And where with His flocks He has gone.

Oh Thou, in whose presence my soul takes delight
On whom in affliction I call;
My comfort by day and my song in the night
My hope, my salvation, my all.
Where dost Thou at noontime reside with Thy sheep
To feed on the pastures of love?
Say why in the valley of death should I weep,
Or lonely the wilderness rove?
hymns.first_line: Oh, why should I wander a stranger from Thee,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 571 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: The Lamb of God
hymns.author: Holy Bible: Matthew 3:1-4; John 1:29
stanzas:
In those days came John the Baptist,
Preaching in the wilderness,
Crying with a loud voice, saying,
“Behold, the Lamb of God,
Which taketh away the sins of the world.”
hymns.first_line: In those days came John the Baptist,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 572 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen

hymns.title: Harpeth Valley
hymns.author: Samuel Longfellow, 1864
stanzas:
Where prophet’s word and martyr’s blood,
And prayers of saints were sown.
We to their labors ent’ring in
Would reap where they have sown.

Oh Thou whose call our hearts has stirred!
To do Thy will we come.
Thrust in our sickles at Thy word
And bear our harvest home.
hymns.first_line: Where prophet’s word and martyr’s blood,
hymns.source: The Sacred Harp, 1991 Edition, no. 573 (words via fasola.org); sung by Sacred Harp Bremen
